name: Soviet montage
summary: A cinema made in the cutting room. Two shots meet and a third meaning appears. Fast cuts, steep angles and typed faces drive the argument of the film.

philosophy.core_thesis: Meaning comes from the collision of shots, not from the content of a single shot, so the edit is the author of the film.
design_principles: Cut at an average shot length of 2 to 3 s (Man with a Movie Camera 2.1 s, Battleship Potemkin 2.8 s on Cinemetrics) and shorten the shots toward a climax.
Join two shots so that their collision makes a third idea: pair the image with its opposite and hold each for 1 to 3 s.
Choose the cut by one of five methods: metric (fixed frame count), rhythmic, tonal, overtonal or intellectual, and keep one method for each sequence.
Shoot from low or high angles of 20° to 45° off level, with diagonals that cross the 1.33:1 frame, and fill the frame with a type, not an individual.
Build a sequence from 8 to 20 shots of a single action seen from many angles, and cut on the peak of the movement.
Use hard daylight on location at high contrast, and print on black and white stock with deep blacks.
Limit the intertitles to 2 to 4 words in a large heavy sans-serif face, 1 to 2 s on screen.
anti_patterns: Long takes of over 8 s with no inner cut
Invisible continuity cuts that hide the edit
A star actor as a psychological individual
Studio sets built for naturalistic depth
A story with no social class or crowd

composition.framing: Steep angles and strong diagonals in a 1.33:1 frame; a face or a machine fills 50% to 80% of the height.
composition.staging_in_depth: A foreground of 2 to 3 m with a machine, a crowd or a stair behind; the layers show a class or a force.
composition.subject_placement: Off centre on a diagonal; the second shot answers the first on the opposite side of the frame.

camera_and_movement.movement: Static for the core of a sequence. Dynamic moves are for a documentary rush: moving vehicle, tracking, split screen, slow and fast motion.
camera_and_movement.support: Tripod, car and tram mounts, crane
camera_and_movement.camera_height: Low from 0.3 m or high from above 3 m; avoid eye level
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Tram or car speed, 5 to 10 m/s, for a rush shot

lens_and_format.frame_rate: 16 to 18 fps capture; project at 18 to 24 fps
lens_and_format.focal_length: 28mm to 75mm (35mm format); a long lens for a compressed crowd
lens_and_format.aperture: f/5.6 to f/8 for sharp faces and machines
lens_and_format.focus: Deep focus on the faces and the machine; no soft background.

light.quality: Hard, high-contrast daylight, steel and water glare, and few filler lamps.
light.direction: Side and back light that rims a face or a machine against a dark ground.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Black and white with deep blacks and a clean white. The only colour is a rare hand-painted red.
grade_recipe: Convert to black and white with a red filter look: red channel at +40%, blue at −30%.
Set the black point at 3% and the white point at 96%.
Add an S-curve of +30% contrast, and keep the midtone at 18% grey.
Hand-paint one accent, such as a flag, at hue 355° in 1 to 3 shots only.
Add grain at 10% and keep the frame edge sharp, with no vignette.

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 2 to 3 s (Cinemetrics: Man with a Movie Camera 2.1 s, Battleship Potemkin 2.8 s)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 0.3 s for a flash cut to 12 s for a held mass shot
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Join by collision, graphic match or rhythm. Shorten the shots by 20% to 50% toward a climax.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut, a flash cut of 4 to 8 frames, a double exposure, a split screen.

sound.approach: The film is silent. The score is built to the rhythm of the cut.
sound.dialogue: Intertitle cards, 2 to 4 words, 1 to 2 s.
sound.music: A percussive, mechanical orchestral score at the pulse of the cut; modern releases use a new score.
sound.loudness: None: silent. A new score for a release sits at −23 LUFS.

titles_and_graphics.treatment: Bold slogans and diagonal type that act as one more shot.
titles_and_graphics.type: Heavy grotesque sans-serif, upper case, on a diagonal at 8° to 15°; white on black or black on red.

shot_primer.opening: Open on a machine or a crowd at a steep angle; the first cut comes inside 2 s.

negative: star close-up with a soft glow

emotion.target_response: Urgency and collective force: the viewer feels a crowd, a machine and a push to act.

use_cases: music video with a hard rhythm
brand film about industry or labour
avoid_when: The brief needs a quiet, character-led scene or a slow mood.
The audience reads a hard political reference as a threat to the brand.

modifiers.how: Keep the cut rhythm at 3 to 5 s and the hard black and white; move to a street, a handheld camera and one named person.
Keep the black and white and the low angles; cut to an average of 6 to 10 s, add one hard key and painted shadows.
